en.name: Nameko
en.summary: Nameko are small amber mushrooms naturally coated in a clear gel, used in miso soup and grated-radish dishes. No figure is published for them, so treat them like mushrooms — but shortened: about 2–4 days refrigerated, because nameko spoils faster than any other cultivated mushroom.
en.pantry: Nameko should never be left at room temperature, not even briefly. Its surface gel holds a great deal of water against the cap, which is exactly the condition bacteria want, and a warm pack goes sour within hours. There is no room-temperature figure and none should be assumed. Buy it from the chiller cabinet and get it home cold.
en.fridge: Keep the sealed pack cold at 4 °C (40 °F) or below and use it soon — about 2–4 days is the working limit, borrowed from the general mushroom figure and shortened because nameko's high surface moisture makes it the most perishable of the group. There is a judging problem worth knowing about: nameko is naturally coated in gel, so the usual slimy-means-spoiled test does not apply. Judge it instead by smell, and by whether the caps have gone brown and mushy rather than firm and amber.
en.freezer: There is no freezer timeline for nameko and we will not invent one. It can be frozen in its pack or bagged flat at −18 °C (0 °F) and dropped into miso soup from frozen, and food at that temperature stays safe indefinitely — but no quality window has been published. Given how quickly nameko goes over in the fridge, freezing the pack on the day you buy it is a reasonable thing to do; just do not treat it as a long-term store.
en.thawing: Do not thaw nameko. Tip it straight from frozen into miso soup or a simmering broth. Thawed nameko loses what structure it has and the gel thins out into the liquid.
spoilage: A sour, fermented or ammonia smell — the most reliable test for this mushroom
Caps gone brown and mushy instead of firm and amber
Cloudy or discoloured liquid in the pack
A puffed or gassy pack, or a date that has passed
tips: Buy nameko last and get it into the fridge fast; it is the least forgiving mushroom there is.
Do not judge it by sliminess — the gel is supposed to be there.
Rinse it briefly only if the recipe asks; the gel is the thickening you want in miso soup.
Freeze the pack on the day you buy it if you will not cook it within a couple of days.

faq.q: How long does nameko last in the fridge?
faq.a: About 2–4 days at 4 °C (40 °F) or below, in the sealed pack. That figure is borrowed from mushrooms generally and shortened, because nameko is the most perishable of them.

faq.q: Nameko is slimy — is it off?
faq.a: Not necessarily. Nameko is naturally coated in a clear gel, so the usual slimy test does not work. Go by smell and by whether the caps are still firm and amber.
No timeline is published, so we do not give one. It freezes at −18 °C (0 °F) and goes straight into miso soup from frozen, which is a reasonable move given how fast it goes over.
Only briefly, and only if a recipe asks. The gel on the surface is what thickens a miso soup pleasantly; rinsing it all away wastes the point of the mushroom.

zh.name: 滑菇
zh.summary: 滑菇是表面天然包覆一層透明膠質的小型琥珀色菇，常用於味噌湯和蘿蔔泥料理。它沒有公布的保存數據，可以比照菇類來看，但要縮短：冷藏約 2～4 天，因為滑菇是所有人工栽培菇裡壞得最快的。
zh.pantry: 滑菇絕對不能放室溫，連一下子都不行。表面的膠質把大量水分鎖在菌傘上，那正是細菌最喜歡的條件，一包回過溫的滑菇幾小時內就會發酸。這裡不提供常溫保存天數，也請不要自行推估。請在冷藏櫃購買並全程保冷帶回家。
zh.fridge: 請保持密封包裝冷藏於 4°C 以下，並盡快用掉——約 2～4 天是工作上限，這是比照菇類整體的數字並往下縮短，因為滑菇表面水分高，是這一群裡最不耐放的。這裡有個值得知道的判斷陷阱：滑菇本來就包著一層膠質，所以「變黏就是壞了」這條常用規則在它身上不成立。請改用氣味判斷，並看菌傘是否還結實呈琥珀色，而不是已經轉褐變糊。
zh.freezer: 滑菇沒有冷凍保存期限，我們也不會自己編一個。它可以連包裝或平鋪裝袋冷凍於 −18°C，使用時不解凍直接丟進味噌湯；食品在該溫度下安全上可無限期保存，只是沒有公布的品質期限。考慮到滑菇在冰箱裡壞得多快，買回來當天就冷凍是很合理的做法，只是不要把它當成長期庫存。
zh.thawing: 滑菇不要解凍。直接從冷凍狀態倒進味噌湯或滾著的高湯裡。解凍後它僅有的結構會散掉，膠質也會稀釋進湯裡。
spoilage: 有酸味、發酵味或阿摩尼亞味——這是這種菇最可靠的判斷方式
菌傘轉褐變糊，而不是結實的琥珀色
包裝內的液體變混濁或變色
包裝鼓脹產氣，或已超過標示日期
tips: 採買時最後才拿，並盡快放進冰箱；它是最不容錯的菇。
不要用「黏不黏」判斷——那層膠本來就該在。
除非食譜要求，否則不用沖洗；那層膠正是味噌湯要的濃稠感。
兩天內煮不完的話，買回來當天就整包冷凍。

faq.q: 滑菇放冰箱可以放多久？
faq.a: 4°C 以下冷藏、保持密封包裝約 2～4 天。這個數字是比照菇類整體並往下縮短，因為滑菇是其中最不耐放的。

faq.q: 滑菇黏黏的是壞掉了嗎？
faq.a: 不一定。滑菇表面本來就有一層透明膠質，所以常用的「變黏就丟」規則不適用。請用氣味判斷，並看菌傘是否還結實呈琥珀色。
沒有公布的期限，所以我們不給數字。它可以冷凍於 −18°C 並不解凍直接下味噌湯；考量到它壞得快，這其實是很合理的做法。
除非食譜要求，否則只要快速沖一下就好。表面那層膠正是讓味噌湯口感變滑順的關鍵，全沖掉就白買了。
